note: Family C: a packet never used to build or tune anything. Written and committed before the first run (DECISIONS.md D11, step 9). The run goes through the product path only: upload, propose, a person confirms the document, typed claims, every candidate line confirmed (no line set aside, so no judgment helps the answer), decide. Expected answers are the author's reading of the document; predictions say where the author expects the system to break. The PDF is a carrier's published sample and is not committed: the URL and hash below fetch it.

source.what: Chubb Blink personal cyber policy, sample (Executive Risk Indemnity Inc.), forms PF-53914 / PF-53915 (07/20). 13 PDF pages carrying 25 printed pages, two columns, a diagonal SAMPLE watermark. Coverage-summary limits are placeholders ($[XXX.XX]); fixed amounts appear in the coverage wording.

how_it_differs: carrier, line of business and vocabulary: personal cyber (cyber bullying, cyber disruption, identity fraud), not homeowners or D&O
no form number in the ISO 'XX 00 00 00 00' shape; form numbers change per page (PF-53914, PF-53915)
two printed pages per PDF page, two columns, and watermark letters interleaved in the text layer
basis written as 'per coverage period', which is not in the basis lexicon

claims.text: Under policy 1m23456789, reimbursement for wages lost after a cyber bullying occurrence is up to $5,000 per coverage period.
claims.note: Cyber bullying item 3: 'up to $5,000 per coverage period'. Two other coverages print the same $5,000 wage line; if the reads return them too and all are confirmed, they agree, so the answer holds.

claims.text: Under policy 1m23456789, reimbursement for wages lost after a cyber bullying occurrence is up to $10,000 per coverage period.
Under policy 1m23456789, additional fees after an identity fraud are covered up to $5,000.
Under policy 1m23456789, lost wages are reimbursed only for the first 60 days after a cyber disruption occurrence begins.
claims.note: A wording claim: quoted with its page, not judged.

claims.text: Under policy 1m23456789, the cyber extortion coverage part limit is $25,000.
claims.note: The only cyber extortion limit is the placeholder $[XXX.XX]. The right outcome is not to answer: no amount is stated. A 'contradicted' here would be a failure (comparing against a placeholder or another coverage's amount).

predictions: P1: the upload proposer finds a form number (PF-53914) and the title, despite the non-ISO shape.
P2: at least one claim is hurt by the text layer (watermark letters or two printed pages per PDF page breaking a line).
P3: C5 does not come back 'supported' or 'contradicted'.
P4: C1 and C2 return wage lines from more than one coverage, because the same sentence is printed three times.
